main_body: A flat snow ground patch (4x3 tiles) of grey-green with pale blue-lavender blobs, white speckles and dark dashes; it is a terrain surface with no standing volume
top_band: none - flat ground texture, no top/front structure
evidence: Terrain ground tile. It is not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. No receding side faces and no elevation drawing. The pattern repeats in a regular grid of lavender blobs.

style.evidence: The ground has about 5 tones: white, pale lavender, mid grey-green, darker grey-green and a dark green-grey. The speckles and dashes add variation, but the layout is a mechanical repeat. The identical lavender blobs with white dot clusters and the dark dashes recur at a fixed interval, which reads as a stamped pattern rather than hand-shaded snow. The lavender blobs are mostly flat fills of about 5x6 px. The grey-green base is dull and does not read as snow, though hue is not judged. The Beodeul grass and paving references have more organic clump and stone shading. Per-tile information is moderate, but the blobs and the repetition keep it below the references. When in doubt, fail.
